solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go over carriage

indicators.note: over signals turning the word for go back to front

parts.note: to go is to part, as in 'we must part now'

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect a railway carriage once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns PART round to give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle is called a trap, an old kind of carriage.

clue.text: Report of patient's progress round home

parts.note: a round of ammunition is a bullet
at home means in

explanation.surface: A hospital update given while doing a ward round of the patient's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals issue short official statements on a patient's condition, called medical bulletins.

clue.text: Bonded, initially, with Italian robber in gang

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word bonded

parts.note: with means and

explanation.surface: An Italian criminal bound into a gang of thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw who robs as one of an armed band is a bandit.

clue.text: Biscuit and alcoholic drink ahead of game

indicators.note: ahead of places the drink before the game in the answer

parts.note: brandy is a spirit distilled from wine
snap is a children's card game

explanation.surface: A biscuit and a glass of something strong before a round of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAP is a card game where players shout 'snap' on spotting a matching pair; a brandy snap is a thin rolled ginger biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy snap is a crisp, lacy rolled biscuit flavoured with ginger, often filled with cream.

clue.text: Shoots fare for the Christmas dinner table?

definitions.text: fare for the Christmas dinner table?

explanation.surface: Young plants that are also part of a festive meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Brussels sprouts are a fixture of the British Christmas dinner, which is what the question mark points to.
explanation.definitionFit: New growths from seeds are shoots; Brussels varieties are traditional festive vegetables in Britain.

clue.text: Promise son clothes

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
wear is a collective word for clothing, as in menswear

explanation.surface: A pledge that a boy will be properly dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To vow or give one's solemn word is to swear.

clue.text: Building stocked remote safety device

indicators.note: building suggests these letters are being put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A remote building kept fully stocked, with a safety gadget installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' rearranges the letters of STOCKED REMOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm that warns of fire by sensing fumes is a common household safety device.

clue.text: In a city that's ancient, I caught Goldfinger

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An archaeologist claims to have nabbed a famous Bond villain in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Goldfinger, the James Bond villain, has the first name Auric, and the word also means golden.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bond villain Goldfinger's first name; the adjective also means made of or like gold.

clue.text: Chapter really upset Scottish historian

indicators.note: upset means the letters of really are knocked into disorder

explanation.surface: A chapter that greatly disturbed a reader of Scottish history.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle was a nineteenth-century Scottish writer of history, author of The French Revolution.

clue.text: Friendly foreign correspondent?

parts.note: not a journalist abroad but an overseas friend one exchanges letters with

explanation.surface: A cordial reporter stationed abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone, often abroad, with whom one keeps up a friendship through letters is a pen friend.

clue.text: Racket, fearful roar outside yard, is normal?

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled roar wraps around the noise
fearful suggests the letters of roar are thrown into disarray

parts.note: a din is a racket or loud noise

explanation.surface: A rowdy, frightening roar heard outside the yard is nothing out of the ordinary?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fearful' makes ORAR, and 'outside' wraps it round the noise; 'is normal?' reads like a question about the racket, but it ends the clue as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normal is usual and unremarkable, which is to say commonplace.

clue.text: Test burger out where impoverished journalists used to meet

definitions.text: where impoverished journalists used to meet

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Trying out a burger in a place where poor hacks once gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TEST BURGER. Grub Street was a London street historically home to struggling hack writers.
explanation.definitionFit: A former London street name, now a byword for needy hack writers and literary drudges.

clue.text: Second-floor family?

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
the floor is the ground

explanation.surface: Asks whether the family lives on the second floor.
explanation.definitionFit: One's background is one's upbringing and social origins, much as one's family.

clue.text: Ma's toy boy, losing head, flipped twice

indicators.note: twice means the resulting pair is written two times
flipped turns the remaining pair of letters round
losing head drops the first letter of the word boy

explanation.surface: A mother's young lover, beheaded, turns head over heels two times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes B from BOY to leave OY; 'flipped' turns it to YO, and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool on a string that climbs and falls is a classic children's plaything.

clue.text: As a result, coin minted — new series

indicators.note: minted suggests coin is freshly struck into a new shape

parts.note: a series is a sequence

explanation.surface: Consequently, a coin is struck for a new series.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means thereby or consequently, describing what follows from something.

clue.text: Huge mines exploded around me

indicators.note: around means the scattered letters surround the other word
exploded suggests the letters of mines are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Enormous mines blowing up all around the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' makes IMNSE from the explosives, and 'around' wraps those letters round the speaker's own word.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge and enormous are near synonyms describing something very large.

clue.text: Greatly affecting winning finish

parts.note: a team that is ahead or winning is said to be up
an ending is a finish

explanation.surface: A victorious conclusion to a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Overturning or turning someone's life upside down greatly affects it.

clue.text: Self-satisfied hint of smile on face

indicators.note: hint of asks for just the first letter of smile

parts.note: mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: A faint smile on someone's face betrays complacency.
explanation.definitionFit: Complacent or self-satisfied people look pleased with themselves.

clue.text: Play with male office worker in trial

indicators.note: in places the man and the worker inside the trial

parts.note: a trial is a test
he is a male pronoun
a temp is a temporary office worker

explanation.surface: A drama about a man and a temporary clerk on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tempest is a play by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Accommodate fool

explanation.surface: A two-word pairing of housing someone and deceiving them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to give lodging to someone and to deceive or trick them.

clue.text: Authoritarian Irish novelist? Sounds like him

indicators.note: sounds like says the writer's name is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Laurence Sterne, author of Tristram Shandy, was born in Ireland

explanation.surface: A question about whether an Irish author was strict, by the sound of his name.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne's surname has a final E that the answer drops.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict, severe or authoritarian manner is stern.

clue.text: Coin kept popping up

indicators.note: popping suggests the letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: A coin I had stored kept springing upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popping' rearranges COIN KEPT; 'up' looks like part of the movement but is the definition, as in being ahead financially.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ahead financially, having made a profit, is to be up on a deal.

clue.text: Completely frustrated, I had returned before she had

indicators.note: before places the turned piece ahead of the next
returned signals the short form of I had is read backwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
she'd is the contraction of she had

explanation.surface: A man tells how he came back before a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the contraction I'd round; 'Completely frustrated' uses the informal British sense of dished, meaning done for.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dished is informal British for being utterly ruined or thwarted.

clue.text: Head of Smithsonian shown with recently stolen picture

indicators.note: head of asks for the first letter of Smithsonian

parts.note: hot goods are recently stolen ones

explanation.surface: A museum chief displays a just-stolen painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph is often called a shot, as in a snapshot.

clue.text: Boredom detected in English nun, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect suggests the letters of nun and I are dubious, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A suspicion that an English nun is weary of convent life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges NUN I as NNUI after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless weariness from lack of interest is what the French loan word means.

clue.text: Find ladder on the ground

parts.note: a ladder in tights is a run
something on the ground is down

explanation.surface: Locating a ladder lying on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a ladder is a run in tights or stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: To track down or locate something after searching is to run it down.
